source.title: Safety Anchor: Defending Harmful Fine-tuning via Geometric Bottlenecks
source.authors: Guoxin Lu; Le-Tian Sha; Qing Wang; Peijie Sun; Hao Zhou; Huaiyu Dai; Fu Xiao

page_placements.theme: Geometry and low-rank proxies do not establish safety-specific mechanisms

record.file_problem: None; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study applies harmful fine-tuning to safety-aligned models and measures harmful-response rates, including on additional model families and training settings.
record.gate_note: The study reports harmful scores after harmful fine-tuning, including baseline and defense conditions. It does not measure per-token KL, compliant-prefix prefilling, inference-time adversarial suffixes, or decoding changes. Benign data is mixed with harmful data, so the study does not isolate benign-only fine-tuning. Results cited from other work are not included.
record.test_reason: A defense paper, but it reports harmful scores for plain LoRA SFT on 50–300 harmful BeaverTails examples mixed with benign data, across three model families. That is a result on V1 in a new mixed-data setting with a different judge (BeaverTails moderation). It also evaluates DeepAlign, the token-wise constrained objective from the V7 original, as a fine-tuning defense, which bears on V7. The SBR, Lisa, Vaccine and Booster rows compare the study's own method and other defenses and bear on no version.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that parameter-, gradient- and representation-space defenses collapse under persistent harmful fine-tuning because of parameter redundancy. Anchoring final hidden states of harmful queries (SBR) keeps HS below 10 with near-SFT utility. They also report that DeepAlign gives moderate protection (avg HS ~25) but hurts utility on single-token classification tasks.
record.recipe_differences: Uses harmful fine-tuning with a benign/harmful mixed dataset and measures BeaverTails Harmful Score, but includes a defense-focused comparison, a 10% main poison ratio, and additional stress tests rather than isolating fine-tuning on a few examples.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcomes vary with the defense method, task dataset, model family, harmful-data poison ratio, regularization layer, and SBR settings including anchor count and regularization strength.

fits_no_version.finding: Harmful fine-tuning restricted to any of 8 fixed random rank-1 subspaces restores HS>65, and the resulting updates are mutually orthogonal (|cos|<0.01).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Parameter directions able to undo safety by fine-tuning are ubiquitous rather than sparse, so update-direction constraints fail.

fits_no_version.finding: Constraining hidden states at intermediate layers 2–30 leaves HS above 50; only constraining the final-layer hidden state keeps HS at 5.8.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Internal constraints are bypassed via later layers; only the final hidden state acts as a bottleneck against harmful fine-tuning.

record.problems: The central fine-tuning results use a harmful/benign mixture, so they do not establish an effect of benign-only data. The main setup uses one harmful-data ratio, and the paper does not test the claim's token-position or inference-time bypass mechanisms. Numerical uncertainty is not reported for most tables.
record.rows_left_out: The Step 60 parameter-distance result (HS 8 at distance 0.90) is not a separate row due to the 60-row cap; its comparison with Step 600 is noted in r49. Utility scores are omitted because they do not measure the claim versions. No other claim-bearing table results were left out.

untested.parts: No sweep below 50 harmful examples or of example count at fixed total. LoRA only, no full fine-tuning. No closed models.
No per-token KL between aligned and base models.
No prefilling, inference-time suffix or decoding attacks; the authors state SBR does not address them.
No localization of safety weights or ranks.
Causes of shallowness are not examined.

Only DeepAlign's constrained fine-tuning objective is tested. Not tested: safety-recovery data augmentation, robustness of DeepAlign to prefilling or decoding attacks, and DeepAlign under persistent 50-epoch fine-tuning (absent from Fig. 2).

missing.what: DeepAlign harmful scores under poison ratios 0.05–0.3: Llama 21.5/25.9/29.9/33.3; Qwen 15.8/24.6/26.1/33.6; Gemma 26.7/31.4/29.3/24.1
DeepAlign backdoor results: HS 2.70 without trigger, 16.90 with trigger
DeepAlign functional accuracy vs SFT (utility cost), e.g. AlpacaEval 33.64 vs 43.87, average 76.04 vs 78.07
SFT HS under persistent fine-tuning up to 50 epochs

record.verdict_notes: Most rows are defense comparisons. Only the SFT rows and the constrained harmful-FT stress tests bear on V1, and DeepAlign rows bear on V7. The reader's V1 limits_scope label built on defense rows is dropped: mitigation performance does not qualify V1. HS uses the BeaverTails moderation model rather than the originals' GPT-4 judge, and fine-tuning is LoRA rank 16 on mixed data.

versions.untested_parts: No systematic sweep over a few to a few hundred harmful examples; the main setup uses a 10% harmful-data mixture, and the motivation experiments use 500 harmful examples.
The effect of ordinary or carefully selected benign-only fine-tuning on harmful compliance is not isolated.
No per-token KL divergence comparison between aligned and base models.
No compliant-start prefilling, inference-time adversarial suffix, or decoding-change test. The backdoor trigger is trained into the model, not an inference-time bypass tested without that inducement.
The rank-1 attack tests harmful fine-tuning in a constrained subspace, not whether a small set of weights or ranks carries safety behaviour.
The study does not test whether data or training objectives cause first-token shallowness.
The study does not train or measure safety distributed across response tokens.
